item.statement: A meth overdose can look like a body in overdrive, with a racing heart and fast breathing.
item.why: The body can also overheat, chest pain can happen, and some people lose touch with reality. That's second-hand, from two reviews of hospital studies, and how often each sign shows up varies a lot.

quiz.reason: Verdict and why are supported, and knowing the signs is practical safety. Form: the why opened with the source and repeated the statement's own signs (racing heart, fast breathing). The fix leads with signs the statement lacks, all from the lines (body getting very hot, chest pain, losing touch with reality), and keeps the 'but' line word for word as the limit. Statement unchanged.

item.statement: Reviews rank MDMA with moclobemide or similar antidepressants as the riskiest mix they list.
item.why: Four young people in Finland died with MDMA and moclobemide in their blood, and pathologists called each death an accidental poisoning with the two drugs. Four deaths can't give a rate, and all four also had other drugs.

quiz.reason: Supported by how line 3 and a strong safety fact framed as risk. 'Antidepressants like moclobemide' can be read as 'antidepressants, for example moclobemide', i.e. any antidepressant, while the lines say only 'this kind of antidepressant'; reworded to 'moclobemide or similar antidepressants'. Why unchanged: supported, and it rightly leaves out the not-prescribed, blood-level and taking-more lines.
